slides.5.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.5.points.0: ✓ Tuscany detail: everyday steak → Chianti; premium aged T-bone → Brunello; wild boar → Vino Nobile; Vin Santo soaked Cantucci is the most native dessert pairing
slides.5.points.1: ✓ Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi is the textbook pairing for Marche's Brodetto di Pesce — minerality + high acid perfectly counters tomato-seafood
slides.5.points.2: ✓ Sagrantino di Montefalco has Italy's highest tannins — only powerful braised dishes like wild boar can balance its intensity
slides.5.points.3: ✓ Campania: Fiano di Avellino + Neapolitan pizza; Greco di Tufo + seafood — ancient Greek varieties find their home in southern Italian cuisine
slides.5.points.4: ✓ Orecchiette con Cime di Rapa + Negroamaro — bitter-on-bitter contrast pairing, Puglia's most traditional combination
slides.5.points.5: ✓ Sicily: Nero d'Avola + grilled tuna steak — tuna is the 'red meat of the sea,' suitable for a full-bodied red
slides.5.points.6: ✓ Sardinia: Cannonau + roast lamb/suckling pig (pastoral culture); Vermentino di Gallura + sea bass (sea breeze meets sea fish)
slides.5.points.7: ✓ Central-South Italy core: the richer the dish, the fuller the wine needed; always look for the same island/region wine first
slides.6.title: 🧠 Central & Southern Italy Pairing Knowledge Check
quiz.0.question: What is the most regionally authentic pairing for Marche's Brodetto di Pesce (tomato seafood stew)?
quiz.0.options.1: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi (Marche white wine)
quiz.0.explanation: Verdicchio is Marche's native variety — its minerality perfectly resonates with Adriatic seafood umami, and its high acidity counters the tomato's sharpness. A textbook example of regional pairing.
quiz.1.question: Why does Sagrantino di Montefalco need a dish as powerful as braised wild boar, and why does it fail with delicate white fish?
quiz.1.options.0: Because Sagrantino's colour is visually unsuited to white fish
quiz.1.options.1: Because Sagrantino has Italy's highest tannins — a delicate dish cannot balance its powerful astringency
quiz.1.options.2: Because Sagrantino must be drunk in Umbria
quiz.1.options.3: Because Sagrantino is too sweet and tastes strange with fish
quiz.1.explanation: Sagrantino's extremely high tannins need to bind to the proteins in meat in order to soften. White fish lacks the protein and fat needed to tame it, making the tannins taste even more aggressively astringent. Weight must match weight.
quiz.2.question: What is the most authentic Sardinian pairing for grilled sea bass (Branzino al Forno)?
quiz.2.explanation: Vermentino di Gallura is Sardinia's only DOCG white wine — its sea-breeze minerality mirrors the fresh sweetness of sea bass. 'Sea breeze meets sea fish' is the finest example of regional pairing.
quiz.3.question: What is the most traditional Tuscan dessert pairing for Vin Santo?
quiz.3.options.2: Cantucci almond biscotti (dipped into Vin Santo)
quiz.3.explanation: Dipping Cantucci into Vin Santo is Tuscany's most traditional dessert culture — the sweet wine softens the hard biscuit, the biscuit absorbs the wine's nutty-caramel aromas. A pure expression of local food culture.
